name: Finishes
description: Preview foil, spot UV, emboss and soft-touch finishes on your artwork - then export the printer-ready spot plate. The on-screen sheen is presentation only; the plate is the real deliverable your print house needs.
a11yLabel: Artwork with a simulated print finish, or the printer-ready finish plate in plate view

featured.blurb: Foil, spot UV and emboss - with the plate your printer needs

inputs.label: Artwork
inputs.help: Pick your artwork or upload your own. It's processed on your device - the pixels never leave the browser.

inputs.label: Finish
inputs.help: The physical finish to simulate. Foils and spot UV fill the mask; emboss and deboss raise or sink its edges; soft-touch mattes everything outside the mask.

inputs.label: Strength
inputs.help: How strongly the finish reads on screen. Preview only - the exported plate is always full-strength ink.

inputs.label: Sheen animation
inputs.help: Sweep a light band across foil and spot UV, like tilting the sheet. Automatically stilled when you prefer reduced motion; stills never bake a mid-sweep frame.

inputs.label: Sweep angle
inputs.help: Direction of the foil grain and sheen sweep.

inputs.label: Mask from
inputs.help: Where the finish goes. Light and dark areas threshold the artwork's perceptual (OKLab) lightness; By colour matches areas near a chosen colour.

inputs.label: Match colour
inputs.help: Areas perceptually close to this colour join the mask.

inputs.label: Threshold
inputs.help: Lightness cut-off (OKLab L) for light/dark masks, or match radius for By colour. Ignored for Whole image.

inputs.label: Edge softness
inputs.help: Feathers the mask edge. 0 is a hard cut - the plate always exports hard-edged either way.

inputs.label: Background
inputs.help: Fill behind the artwork when it doesn't cover the frame.

inputs.label: Plate view (printer-ready)
inputs.help: Switch to the deliverable: the finish mask as pure black on white with an overprint label. Send THIS to your print house - the shiny preview is presentation only and must never be baked into artwork.
